The physics engine switches on. Nothing in this project has a collider or a rigidbody - today you give the player a body, and find out that it changes the whole game.

Tue Sep 222.2
2.2 — Spikes: Physics, Damage & DeathBuild Lab
CED AAP-3, AAP-2, CRD-2

The pivotal lesson of the unit. A solid spike reveals that transform.Translate has made your character a ghost - so you choose a movement method you can live with all year, then build health and death on top of it.

Wed Sep 302.5
2.5 — Physics & Stats Studio: Catch Up and TuneBuild Lab
CED AAP-2, AAP-3, CRD-2

The heaviest unit gets a day to settle. Finish 2.1-2.4 if you are behind, re-tune your movement now that a physics body is doing the work, and fix the top item from your playtest notes.

Fri Oct 22.6
Unit 2 Review + Second PlaytestStudio
CED CRD-2, AAP-2
  • 2.62.6 Unit 2 Review + Second PlaytestBuild Lab
  • 2.72.7 Refactor Day: Moving Stats into the StatManagerBuild Lab

Swap seats and playtest again now that your fixes have landed. Compare the two sheets - did the fix actually work? Close the unit by demonstrating your spike, your potion and your death rule. Then the refactor: coins, health and the ceiling leave PlayerController and move onto the StatManager singleton that has been an empty stub since September. Nothing the game does changes - only who owns the numbers.

Wed Oct 284.4
Attack: Close-Range Contact DamageLesson
CED AAP-2
  • 4.44.4 Attack: Close-Range Contact DamageBuild Lab
  • 4.64.6 Player Melee: A Hitbox That Remembers the EnemyBuild Lab

The enemy hits you; then you hit back. A sprite child with a BoxCollider2D, moved to the side you are facing. Whatever it touches is stored in a variable, and the swing calls ChangeHealth(int amount) on it - the first time your player does something to the world instead of the world doing something to the player.

Thu Nov 125.3
5.3 — Into the Cave: Persistence & the HUDBuild Lab
CED AAP-1, CRD-2

The architectural payoff. Leaving the overworld destroys every stat the student owns, because a scene load replaces rather than loses. The StatManager from 2.7 is the answer; today they verify it does its three jobs - one original, surviving the load, and clamping - and then build the HUD that shows health and coins where the game begins.
